text:
maria_support: Hey team, escalating a live customer issue — they started seeing intermittent 429s for a production app after a sudden traffic spike. Customer claims most requests hit us from eu-west but some requests are routed to us-west and that's when they get 429s. They see <x-region> headers alternating and a bunch of `x-rate-limit-remaining: 0` in the responses.

maria_support: Quick summary from customer: 30s window of burst, baseline 50rps -> spike to ~800rps for ~45s. Error rate jumped ~8% during spike, primarily 429s. Logs attached by customer show request ids and a few 401s mixed in (they rotated an API key right before the spike but think 401s are unrelated).

jyoti_oncall: thanks — can you paste one example of the raw response headers and a request-id? also was this on Dedicated or Hosted? any dedicated pool id?

maria_support: Hosted API. Example response (redacted):

```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-request-id: r-8b3f9c2e
x-region: us-west-2
x-fallback-region: eu-west-1
x-rate-limit-limit: 100
x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-rate-limit-reset: 14
content-type: application/json
```

maria_support: Customer also sent their client request trace: most requests have `x-client-region: eu-west-1` but we see `x-region: us-west-2` on some replies. They suspect our cross-region failover is draining into the destination region's quota and causing cross-region throttles.

kevin_sre: @maria_support that pattern matches a per-region quota enforcement + cross-region fallback. If eu-west was saturated it can route to us-west where the request hits us-west's capacity and its rate limiter. If us-west has lower leftover quota the client would see 429s. Do we have the customer's org id? need to check per-org per-region quota counters.

maria_support: org-id: org_79b2 (provided by customer). Customer also included a curl repro we can run to simulate:

```
for i in {1..600}; do 
  curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{redirect_url} %{url_effective}\n" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \
    -H "x-client-region: eu-west-1" \
    "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" &
done
wait
```

maria_support: they saw ~4-5% 429s locally when running that loop from a eu-west VM with concurrency ~100.

jyoti_oncall: can you dump a few `x-server-*` headers from the 429 responses? we want the backend pool id + the router decision trace. also include the request ids so we can map to logs.

maria_support: pasted three request ids: r-8b3f9c2e, r-8b3f9f44, r-8b3fa101. Here is one 429 response body from customer (sanitized):

```
{"error": {"type":"rate_limit","message":"region quota exceeded","region":"us-west-2","retry_after":12}}
```

maria_support: note: customer rotated keys around the same time so they also saw a handful of 401s. They confirmed those were from an older key; nothing to do with routing. Billing: they also hit their monthly committed usage and got throttled to free-tier limits? not sure — @elaine_billing can you confirm if org_79b2 had any billing hold or credit exhaustion at the exact time?

elaine_billing: checking ledger.. org_79b2 consumed committed capacity earlier today and their usage crossed into overage at 2026-03-03T10:12:03Z — we sent a notice but did not cut access; no payment hold. Their billing profile is pay-as-you-go with overage enabled. So billing likely not the immediate cause.

kevin_sre: good to know. So likely behavior: traffic spikes in eu-west, router tries local region; when local capacity exhausted we fallback to another region (us-west) — fallback respects destination region quotas, not aggregate. If destination is low on spare capacity you get 429s. Our router currently does naive cross-region fanout on overload. We have safeguards but not a combined global quota view.

kevin_sre: immediate mitigation options:
- temporary emergency bump on org_79b2 quotas in us-west and eu-west (quick action from ops)
- add a short-lived routing preference for that org to prefer eu-west-only (avoid cross-region fallback)
- advise customer to smooth the spike (client-side concurrency limit) and retry with exponential backoff based on `retry_after`

maria_support: customer asked for a repro we can run from our infra to reproduce without them. @jyoti_oncall can you run the curl loop from an eu-west machine in infra and capture headers?

jyoti_oncall: running now — will post back with results. also grabbing router traces.

deploy-bot: Deploy started: patch/route-weighting-2026-03-03 -> staging (commit abc123).

jyoti_oncall: ran the loop, reproduced ~3.9% 429s. Router trace for r-8b3f9c2e: `router->decision: prefer eu-west (saturated) -> fallback us-west-2 (selected candidate) -> rate-limiter(us-west-2, org_79b2) rejected`

jyoti_oncall: attached sample backend logs showing per-region counters: `eu-west-1: allocated 120/120 tokens`, `us-west-2: allocated 98/100 tokens` right before spike. When fallback started, us-west dropped to 0 remaining for this org and started returning 429s.

kevin_sre: next steps agreed:
1) ops to apply emergency quota bump in us-west for org_79b2 + short-term delta in eu-west to absorb current traffic (action: @kevin_sre)
2) temporarily set routing for org_79b2 to `region_preference: eu-west-1` to avoid cross-region fallback (action: @jyoti_oncall)
3) engineering to explore a unified global quota view or graceful fallbacks that probe destination quota before full failover (action: eng-runtime, create ticket)
4) support to advise customer on client-side backoff and to confirm key rotation didn't cause auth problems (action: @maria_support)

maria_support: customer accepted temp bump and will throttle on their side too. I'll coordinate timings. Can someone confirm ETA for the ops bump?

kevin_sre: I'll put the quota bump in now and monitor for 15 minutes; will post when done.

kevin_sre: quota bump applied at 1783951420 — increased us-west-2 spare tokens by +300 for org_79b2. Monitoring shows 429 rate drop to <0.5% within 2 minutes.

maria_support: customer confirmed errors subsided after the bump. They also want clarity in docs about cross-region fallback semantics and per-region quotas. Can we get a short blurb for docs/product?

kevin_sre: yes, engineering should add: "Routing may fallback to other regions when local capacity is exhausted. Quotas and rate limits are enforced per-region; fallback consumes the destination region's quota and may be throttled if that region lacks spare capacity." I'll open a GH issue for routing changes and a docs ticket.

elaine_billing: logged a note on the billing side: although billing didn't block, we'll add a proactive alert to customers when they approach committed capacity to avoid surprise overages causing unexpected throttling patterns in weird traffic shapes.

maria_support: thanks all. I'll close the support ticket once eng has a timeline for the router change and docs blurb. Leaving thread open for any follow-ups. :thumbsup:
